intro: These three set a point on a timeline. を皮切りに is the first of a series, with more of the same to follow. を限りに is the last time, after which something stops. を機に is a chance that someone seizes to begin something new. All three follow a noun and belong to formal or written Japanese.

skills.rule: A を皮切りに B: A is the first in a series, and similar events follow one after another.
skills.explain:
皮切り was the first moxa burn of a treatment, so を皮切りに (also を皮切りにして, を皮切りとして) marks the opening event of a chain: a tour starting in Tokyo, the first shop of an expanding chain, the first remark that set off a flood of others. B describes the series spreading or growing: 全国で, 次々と, 各地に.

There must be a sequence in time. A single event that leads to a single change is を機に. A static list of members, with no sequence, is をはじめ: 東京をはじめ、大阪にも店がある.

It marks a beginning, so it is the opposite of を限りに, which marks the end.
patterns: [first event / first place] を皮切りに、[similar events follow / spread]

examples.jp: 東京[とうきょう]公演[こうえん]{を皮切[かわき]りに}、全国[ぜんこく]ツアーが始[はじ]まる。
examples.en: Starting with a show in Tokyo, a nationwide tour will begin.

examples.jp: この店[みせ]は大阪[おおさか]{を皮切[かわき]りに}、全国[ぜんこく]に店舗[てんぽ]を広[ひろ]げた。
examples.en: Starting with Osaka, this chain has spread its branches across the country.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の発言[はつげん]{を皮切[かわき]りに}、次々[つぎつぎ]と反対[はんたい]意見[いけん]が出[で]た。
examples.en: His remark was the first of a string of objections.

examples.jp: シンガポール店[てん]の開店[かいてん]{を皮切[かわき]りに}、アジア各地[かくち]に次々[つぎつぎ]と出店[しゅってん]した。
examples.en: Beginning with the opening of a store in Singapore, they opened stores all over Asia one after another.

examples.jp: 来月[らいげつ]、札幌[さっぽろ]{を皮切[かわき]りにして}、全国[ぜんこく]十[じゅう]の都市[とし]で展示会[てんじかい]を開[ひら]く。
examples.en: Next month the exhibition opens in Sapporo, the first of ten cities around the country.

contrast.note: を機に: one event is the chance for one new start (結婚を機に引っ越した). を皮切りに: the first of many similar events.
をはじめ names the leading member of a group that exists side by side. を皮切りに names the first event in a sequence over time.
を限りに marks the last time; を皮切りに marks the first.

mistakes.bad: 東京[とうきょう]{を皮切[かわき]りに}、大阪[おおさか]や京都[きょうと]にも店[みせ]がある。
mistakes.good: 東京[とうきょう]{をはじめ}、大阪[おおさか]や京都[きょうと]にも店[みせ]がある。
mistakes.note: Shops that simply exist form a list, not a sequence: をはじめ.

mistakes.bad: 結婚[けっこん]{を皮切[かわき]りに}、たばこをやめた。
mistakes.good: 結婚[けっこん]{を機[き]に}、たばこをやめた。
mistakes.note: One event prompting one change is を機に; nothing is a series here.

skills.tip: Can you add "and then one after another"? Then を皮切りに.

skills.rule: [time] を限りに B: with this time as the last, B ends or stops.
skills.explain:
を限りに follows a time word that marks a cut-off: 今日, 本日, 今月, 今年度, 今回, 今シーズン. B is something that stops after that point: quitting a habit, closing a shop, retiring, ending a service. It is common in announcements and personal resolutions: 今日を限りにたばこをやめる.

It marks an end, never a start. The noun is the time or occasion chosen as the last one (今大会を限りに引退する), never a past turning point. A past event after which things changed is を境に: あの日を境に彼は変わった.

をもって is the formal near-equivalent for an end (本日をもって閉店いたします), but unlike を限りに it can also mark a start: 四月一日をもって施行する.

The idiom 声を限りに means "at the top of one's voice" and is not a time use.
patterns: [今日 / 本日 / 今月 / 今回] を限りに、[stop / close / retire]

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]{を限[かぎ]りに}、たばこをやめます。
examples.en: As of today, I am giving up smoking for good.

examples.jp: この店[みせ]は今月[こんげつ]{を限[かぎ]りに}閉店[へいてん]します。
examples.en: This shop will close at the end of this month.

examples.jp: 本日[ほんじつ]{を限[かぎ]りに}、受付[うけつけ]を終了[しゅうりょう]いたします。
examples.en: Today is the last day we accept applications.

examples.jp: 山田[やまだ]選手[せんしゅ]は今[こん]シーズン{を限[かぎ]りに}引退[いんたい]する。
examples.en: Yamada will retire at the end of this season.

examples.jp: この大会[たいかい]は今回[こんかい]{を限[かぎ]りに}廃止[はいし]される。
examples.en: This tournament will be discontinued after this one.

contrast.note: をもって also ends things (本日をもって閉店) and is more formal, but it can mark a start too. を限りに only ever marks the last time.
を境に is a dividing line between before and after, usually an event, with a change of state: あの事故を境に彼は変わった. を限りに is a chosen end point.
を皮切りに is the first of a series; を限りに is the last.

mistakes.bad: 四月[しがつ]{を限[かぎ]りに}、新[あたら]しい制度[せいど]が始[はじ]まる。
mistakes.good: 四月[しがつ]{から}、新[あたら]しい制度[せいど]が始[はじ]まる。
mistakes.note: を限りに marks an end, never a beginning.

mistakes.bad: あの事故[じこ]{を限[かぎ]りに}、彼[かれ]は車[くるま]に乗[の]らなくなった。
mistakes.good: あの事故[じこ]{を境[さかい]に}、彼[かれ]は車[くるま]に乗[の]らなくなった。
mistakes.note: An event that splits life into before and after, with a change that just happened, is を境に; を限りに is a time chosen as the last occasion.

skills.tip: Does "and never again after that" fit, with a time word before the blank? Then を限りに.

skills.rule: A を機に B: taking event A as the opportunity, someone starts or changes B.
skills.explain:
機 means "opportunity". を機に (also を機として) follows a noun for an event in someone's life or an organisation's history: 結婚, 就職, 転勤, 退職, 入院, 創立五十周年. A clause takes の: 入院したのを機に. B is a deliberate new step: moving house, quitting, starting, renaming.

Because someone seizes a chance, B is a decision, not something that just happens. A change with no one deciding, like weather or a mood, is を境に.

をきっかけに is a close neighbour and often works as well. It is more conversational and can also name an accidental or negative trigger for any outcome (喧嘩をきっかけに仲が悪くなった), where を機に sounds wrong. を皮切りに needs a series to follow; を機に is one chance and one change.

examples.jp: 結婚[けっこん]{を機[き]に}、仕事[しごと]を辞[や]めた。
examples.en: I left my job when I got married.

examples.jp: 就職[しゅうしょく]{を機[き]に}、一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしを始[はじ]めました。
examples.en: I started living on my own when I got a job.

examples.jp: 入院[にゅういん]したの{を機[き]に}、父[ちち]は酒[さけ]をやめた。
examples.en: My father took his hospital stay as the occasion to give up drinking.

examples.jp: 定年[ていねん]退職[たいしょく]{を機[き]に}、夫婦[ふうふ]で田舎[いなか]に引[ひ]っ越[こ]した。
examples.en: On retiring, the couple moved to the countryside.

examples.jp: 創立[そうりつ]五十周年[ごじっしゅうねん]{を機[き]に}、社名[しゃめい]を変更[へんこう]いたしました。
examples.en: To mark our fiftieth anniversary, we have changed the company name.

contrast.note: を皮切りに opens a series of similar events. を機に is a single chance taken for a single new step.
を境に is a dividing line between two states and needs no one's decision: 十月を境に寒くなった. を機に needs someone choosing to act.
を限りに sets a time as the last occasion for something; を機に is the occasion for starting something new.

mistakes.bad: 十月[じゅうがつ]{を機[き]に}、急[きゅう]に寒[さむ]くなった。
mistakes.good: 十月[じゅうがつ]{を境[さかい]に}、急[きゅう]に寒[さむ]くなった。
mistakes.note: Nobody seized a chance; weather changing at a dividing point is を境に.

mistakes.bad: 東京[とうきょう]公演[こうえん]{を機[き]に}、全国[ぜんこく]十[じゅっ]か所[しょ]を回[まわ]る。
mistakes.good: 東京[とうきょう]公演[こうえん]{を皮切[かわき]りに}、全国[ぜんこく]十[じゅっ]か所[しょ]を回[まわ]る。
mistakes.note: A first show followed by many more is a series: を皮切りに.

skills.tip: Can you say "took the opportunity of A to ..."? Then を機に.
